Mohamed Soliman

PhD candidate, Mechanical Engineering · Southern Methodist University · expected May 2027

I build closed-form models of how layered structures bend, creep and slip at their interfaces, and I check each one against finite elements and published results. My earlier work covers elastoplastic damage and contact problems, and my current preliminary work applies topology optimization, with heat transfer analysis, to multi-layered structures under mechanical load and heat. I am looking for a postdoctoral position in solid and computational mechanics.

ResearchNewest first

2026PreliminaryTopology optimization

Topology optimization of multi-layered structures under load and heat

A new line of work, separate from the sponsored projects. Each layer of a stack gets its own material layout, and the design is driven by mechanical loading together with heat transfer. The code is density-based with filtering and projection, adjoint sensitivities, a custom method of moving asymptotes solver, aggregated constraints on stress and temperature, and a connectivity constraint for the heat path.

  • Designs that minimize compliance deflect 2.1 to 5.2 times more than the solid reference. Designs that minimize deflection cut the largest deflection to between 0.037 and 0.167 of the solid case and keep compliance at 0.74 to 0.98 of it.
  • Maximum von Mises stress rises to 1.02 to 2.13 times the solid case, because stress is not constrained in these runs.
  • Verification: compliance agrees to about 3×10⁻⁴ and the adjoint sensitivities to about 7.5×10⁻⁶.
2025–2026In preparationSize effects

Size-dependent models for multi-layered plates

The second phase of my dissertation moves from classical to nonclassical elasticity, so that thin layers at micro and nano scales are not modelled as if size did not matter. One model covers perfectly bonded circular plates under axisymmetric thermomechanical loading, built on Kirchhoff plate theory and the modified couple stress theory. A second covers imperfectly bonded rectangular plates on a Pasternak-Winkler foundation. Preliminary results from both agree with finite element simulations and published studies. No paper from this work has been submitted yet.

2026Math. Mech. SolidsElastic foundation

Imperfectly bonded layers on an elastic foundation

A model for structures with any number of imperfectly bonded layers resting on a Winkler foundation, under general thermomechanical loading. A state-space method gives the full response, and closed forms are derived for two- and three-layer structures and for a seven-layer transistor. Results are checked against COMSOL and against an earlier model for the case without a foundation (Shaat et al., 2023).

2026Mech. Mater. 221Imperfect interfaces + creep

Creep in imperfectly bonded multi-layered structures

Layers are allowed to slip through a spring-like interface of prescribed stiffness, and each layer creeps by Norton's power law. The creep-free response at t = 0 is a closed-form solution that comes from recasting the interfacial shear equations as a quadratic eigenvalue problem, a tool from structural dynamics, so it works for any number of layers. The response for t > 0 is marched in time with finite differences. The model predicts interfacial shear and normal stresses including the free-edge zone, and it reduces to earlier solutions as limiting cases.

  • Two-layer case matches Chen et al. (2009); three-layer case matches COMSOL. Raising the interfacial stiffness recovers the perfect-bond result.
  • Shear stress relaxes with creep while interfacial normal stress grows. Both rise sharply at the free edges.
2025Compos. Struct. 370Creep

Creep in perfectly bonded multi-layered structures

An extended Bernoulli-Euler beam model that keeps the Poisson effect, so narrow and wide beams are both covered, with Norton creep in each layer and any number of layers. It predicts how curvature, axial stress and interfacial stresses evolve with time. Validated against Chen et al. for two layers and against COMSOL for a five-layer solid oxide fuel cell over 5000 hr. Creep lowers the axial stress in the layers with high creep-rate constants, while the outer layers see it rise.

2022Zagazig UniversityM.Sc. thesis

Damage evolution in mechanical contact systems

For my master's work I wrote an iterative residual-based procedure for coupled elastoplastic damage problems. It keeps the symmetric part of the coupled tangent in the stiffness matrix and treats the unsymmetric part as a residual force, which substantially reduced solution time and storage. It was implemented in FORTRAN (NAS2D, my own 2D finite element code) and as Abaqus UMAT subroutines, then extended to frictional contact with a variational contact model. Six contact problems were analysed.

  • Damage lowers contact pressure and von Mises stress and enlarges the contact area. Friction raises contact stresses.
  • A fillet instead of a sharp corner reduces damage with little effect on contact pressure.
